title: Positive division remainder and smaller late shift in the full-B2 bound

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"The single total deterministic-field family defined by proof.md and family.py. At actual length N enumerate primes2<=k<=N, r=ceil(N/k) and r-1 with r>=3,k>r+1, m=min(N,rk), ignored p=N-m, and2<=t<r. Use d=H+E0+1 from disperser.md Sections12--13, B=t(t+3)/2<=d<m, and choose the minimum(4p+8d-4B-3,k,t,p) including the zero option(4N,0,0,0). Construct Q_k by the supplied deterministic prime-degree specialization of Shoup in proof.md Appendix A and irreducible_prime(k), ignore p actual input bits, and evaluate the descending-power order-t symmetric polynomial on the remaining m bits over F2[Z]/Q_k with zero padding. No field-polynomial bits or advice are inputs.","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"This ONE fixed total uniform P language, hence NP with empty witnesses, satisfies C_B2(F_N)>=4N-L_N for every integer N>=0 and L_N=O(N^(4/5)), with the exact selector and full pinned B2 convention in proof.md. Hence liminf over ALL integer lengths N of C_B2(F_N)/N>=4. At EVERY integer N>=2^20, C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(11488091/1000000)N^(4/5)+(3276349/500000)N^(3/5)-(995217/50000)N^(2/5)-21. At EVERY integer N>=2^65 it also satisfies C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(11488091/1000000)N^(4/5)+(655026/100000)N^(3/5). Section9.5 proves the new finite refinements using tighter enclosing guards and exact endpoint inequalities. Complete field construction, affine disperser degree, unrestricted gate elimination and all-length coverage are supplied; no prior verdict is a premise. Section9.6 further proves at EVERY integer N>=2^20: C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(11488091/1000000)N^(4/5)+(3276349/500000)N^(3/5)-(995217/50000)N^(2/5)+(45991/10000)N^(1/5)-29, retaining the exact positive adjacent-choice division remainder. Section9.7 improves the N^(2/5) coefficient in that last bound to985621/50000 at EVERY N>=2^65, and proves the simpler bound4N-(11488091/1000000)N^(4/5)+(655029/100000)N^(3/5) on that same late domain.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}

claims: For every ODD PRIME k>=3, the exact irreducible_prime(k) algorithm in family.py terminates in polynomial time in k and outputs a monic irreducible binary polynomial of degree k. proof.md Appendix A supplies the complete prime-degree construction and proof, including binary factor extraction, cyclotomic nonresidue lifting, Kummer extension and trace descent. This specializes a known Shoup construction and does not claim a new general irreducible-construction algorithm.

The complete finite certified losses(original,weighted,positive-exact,zero-deficit,compressed,new) are(1461,1437,1429,1413,1393,1257) at N=500,(2533,2493,2485,2485,2465,2265) at N=1000,(4513,4449,4433,4417,4397,4061) at N=2000,and(16809,16601,16577,16521,16501,15365) at N=10000. These compare certified losses, not actual optimal circuit sizes.

For EVERY integer N>=0 the SAME fixed uniform P family satisfies C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(11488091/1000000)N^(4/5). Sections8--10 supply the full finite floor/error/prime proof, zero range,3784checked intervals for196..2^28-1,8222prime-chain entries and analytic tail. Every real/integer transfer is proved.

For EVERY integer N>=2^27 the SAME fixed uniform P family satisfies C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(11488091/1000000)N^(4/5)+6N^(3/5). The target already enumerates j=floor(sqrt(r)) and j+1; Section9 proves that one has original threshold at most H+k*sqrt(r)-k/2-r^(3/2)/4+k/(4sqrt(r))+r/4+1. Complete guards, adjacent-choice proof, normalized g1/K1 estimates and exact constants are supplied. Bounded checks are sanity checks, not the universal premise. Section9.2 supplies every additional earlier-length guard and prime coverage argument.

For EVERY integer N>=2^20 the SAME fixed uniform P family satisfies C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(11488091/1000000)N^(4/5)+(655269/100000)N^(3/5)-(997/50)N^(2/5)-21. In particular it satisfies C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(11488091/1000000)N^(4/5)+(26201/4000)N^(3/5) at EVERY integer N>=2^65. Section9 supplies the biased adjacent-choice estimate, B>=r/2, exact square-root bounds for K/G3 and the shifted-choice proof, all relaxed guards and both universal transfers. Bounded cases are sanity checks, not the universal proof. Section9.2 proves the earlier-length extension universally. Section9.3 supplies the denser-prime and revised-shift proof for every additional length. Section9.4 supplies the sharper endpoint constants and late corollary. Section9.5 additionally proves: At EVERY integer N>=2^20, C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(11488091/1000000)N^(4/5)+(3276349/500000)N^(3/5)-(995217/50000)N^(2/5)-21. At EVERY integer N>=2^65 it also satisfies C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(11488091/1000000)N^(4/5)+(655026/100000)N^(3/5). Section9.6 further proves at EVERY integer N>=2^20: C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(11488091/1000000)N^(4/5)+(3276349/500000)N^(3/5)-(995217/50000)N^(2/5)+(45991/10000)N^(1/5)-29, retaining the exact positive adjacent-choice division remainder. Section9.7 improves the N^(2/5) coefficient in that last bound to985621/50000 at EVERY N>=2^65, and proves the simpler bound4N-(11488091/1000000)N^(4/5)+(655029/100000)N^(3/5) on that same late domain.
